title: Informative image missing alt attribute
explanation: An img element with no alt attribute gives screen reader users no information, and many read out the file name instead. Informative images need a text alternative that conveys the same information. Purely decorative images should use alt="".
how_to_test_manually: Turn images off or inspect each img element for a meaningful alt, or alt="" when decorative.

title: Image button missing alternative text
explanation: An input of type image acts as a submit button, so its alt text is its accessible name. Without it the control is announced as unlabeled.
how_to_test_manually: Inspect each input type=image and confirm alt describes the action, not the picture.

title: SVG with role img has no accessible name
fail_html: <svg role="img" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10" fill="#0a7d3c"/></svg>
pass_html: <svg role="img" aria-label="Status: online" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10" fill="#0a7d3c"/></svg>
explanation: Inline SVG exposed with role=img must have a name from aria-label, aria-labelledby, or a title element. Otherwise assistive technology announces an unnamed graphic.
how_to_test_manually: Inspect meaningful inline SVGs for a computed accessible name; hide decorative SVGs with aria-hidden="true".

title: Emoji used as an image without a label
explanation: Any element with role=img needs an accessible name. Without one, the emoji is announced inconsistently or ignored.
how_to_test_manually: Search for role=img elements and confirm each has a text alternative.

title: Alt text is a file name instead of a description
explanation: A present alt attribute does not mean it is useful. File names, 'image', and 'photo' are common failures that automated tools usually cannot judge.
how_to_test_manually: Read the alt text aloud. It should communicate the purpose of the image in context.

title: Prerecorded video without a captions track
pass_html: <video controls width="320" height="180"><source src="https://example.com/demo.mp4" type="video/mp4"><track kind="captions" src="https://example.com/demo.en.vtt" srclang="en" label="English"></video>
explanation: Deaf and hard of hearing users need synchronized captions for speech and meaningful sounds. A video element with no captions track is an immediate failure. Note that a track element existing does not guarantee the captions are accurate.
how_to_test_manually: Play the video muted and check caption accuracy, timing, and speaker identification.

title: List built with divs inside a ul
explanation: A ul may only contain li children (and script-supporting elements). Anything else breaks the list semantics screen readers announce, such as 'list with 2 items'.
how_to_test_manually: Inspect list markup and confirm only li elements are direct children of ul and ol.

title: Fake list made of bullet characters
explanation: Typing a bullet character and a line break looks like a list but exposes none of the list structure to assistive technology.
how_to_test_manually: Use a screen reader or accessibility tree view and check that visual lists are exposed as lists.

title: Heading faked with a styled div
fail_html:
Pricing

Choose the plan that fits your team.
pass_html:
Pricing

Choose the plan that fits your team.
explanation: Visual styling alone does not create a heading. Screen reader users navigate by heading level, so visual headings must be real h1 to h6 elements.
how_to_test_manually: Open the screen reader headings list and compare it with the visual headings on the page.

title: Paragraph styled as a heading with bold text only
fail_html:
Shipping options

Delivery takes three to five business days.
pass_html:
Shipping options

Delivery takes three to five business days.
explanation: A short bold paragraph that acts as a section title should be a heading element. This is an experimental axe rule, so treat results as hints.
how_to_test_manually: Look for bold or large text that introduces a section but is not a heading.

title: Data table header row built from td elements
explanation: Without th cells, screen readers cannot tell users which header applies to a data cell. Bold td cells look like headers but carry no semantics.
how_to_test_manually: Navigate the table with a screen reader and confirm column and row headers are announced with each cell.

title: Radio group without fieldset and legend
fail_html: Shipping speed
pass_html: Shipping speed
explanation: A group of related controls needs a programmatic group name. Without a legend, a screen reader user hears 'Standard, radio button' with no clue what the question is.
how_to_test_manually: Tab into the first radio button with a screen reader and confirm the group name is announced.

title: Label for attribute does not match the input id
explanation: A typo between the label for attribute and the input id leaves the field unlabeled even though a label appears next to it.
how_to_test_manually: Click each visible label. The associated input should receive focus.

title: Heading levels skip from h1 to h4
explanation: Heading levels should only increase by one, so users who navigate by heading understand the page outline. Axe reports this as a best practice rather than a strict WCAG failure.
how_to_test_manually: List headings with a screen reader or browser extension and review the outline.

title: Invalid scope value on a table header
explanation: The scope attribute only accepts row, col, rowgroup, and colgroup. The word 'column' is invalid and ignored by assistive technology.
how_to_test_manually: Validate scope values in table markup.

title: CSS order makes visual sequence differ from DOM order
fail_html:
Step 2: Confirm your email address.

Step 1: Create your account.
pass_html:
Step 1: Create your account.

Step 2: Confirm your email address.
explanation: Screen readers and keyboard focus follow DOM order, not CSS order. When visual order carries meaning, the source order has to match it.
how_to_test_manually: Disable CSS or read the page with a screen reader and compare the order to the visual layout.

title: Instruction relies on color and position only
fail_html: Press the green button on the right to continue.
pass_html: Press the Continue button to proceed.
explanation: Users who cannot see color, or whose layout reflows on mobile, cannot follow instructions that depend on how something looks or where it sits.
how_to_test_manually: Read instructions and check they name controls by label, not by color, shape, or position.

title: Invalid autocomplete token on an email field
explanation: Autocomplete tokens must come from the HTML specification. A typo disables the browser and assistive technology features that rely on input purpose.
how_to_test_manually: Check autocomplete tokens on fields that collect the user's own data.

title: Email field missing the autocomplete attribute
explanation: WCAG 1.3.5 requires fields that collect the user's own information to declare their purpose. Axe checks that tokens are valid but does not flag a missing attribute, so this is a gap in automated coverage.
how_to_test_manually: List fields that collect personal data and confirm each has an appropriate autocomplete token.

title: Inline link distinguished only by a slight color change
fail_html: Read our pricing policy before you buy.
pass_html: Read our pricing policy before you buy.
explanation: Links in running text must be distinguishable by more than color, unless the color contrast between link and surrounding text is at least 3:1. Underlines are the most reliable fix.
how_to_test_manually: View the page in grayscale and confirm links are still identifiable.

title: Audio autoplays with no controls
explanation: Audio that starts on its own and lasts more than three seconds interferes with screen readers and needs a visible pause or volume control.
how_to_test_manually: Load the page with speakers on and confirm nothing plays automatically without controls.

title: Light gray body text on a white background
fail_html: Your order ships within two business days.
pass_html: Your order ships within two business days.
explanation: Text of #999999 on white has a contrast ratio of about 2.8:1, well under the 4.5:1 required for normal text.
how_to_test_manually: Measure contrast with a color picker tool. Include hover, focus, disabled, and text over images.

title: White button label on a yellow background
explanation: White on bright yellow has a contrast ratio of roughly 1.4:1. Dark text on yellow passes easily.
how_to_test_manually: Measure button label contrast against button background in all states.

title: Viewport meta disables pinch zoom
explanation: user-scalable=no blocks low vision users from enlarging text on mobile devices. Remove it.
how_to_test_manually: On a phone, try to pinch-zoom the page.

title: Viewport meta caps maximum scale at 1
explanation: A maximum-scale below 2 prevents users from zooming to 200 percent on devices that honor it.
how_to_test_manually: Inspect the viewport meta tag for user-scalable=no or a low maximum-scale.

title: Fixed-width container forces horizontal scrolling at 320px
fail_html: This container is fixed at 1200 pixels wide.
explanation: Content must fit a 320 CSS pixel wide viewport without horizontal scrolling. Fixed pixel widths are the most common cause of reflow failures. Axe cannot test this, but a script can measure scroll width at 320 pixels.
how_to_test_manually: Set the browser window to 320 CSS pixels wide, or zoom to 400 percent at 1280 pixels, and scroll.

title: Text input with a very faint border
explanation: When a border is the only visual cue that a field exists, it needs at least 3:1 contrast against the surrounding background. #dddddd on white is about 1.3:1. Axe does not test non-text contrast.
how_to_test_manually: Measure the contrast of input borders, icons, and control states against their surroundings.

title: Inline line-height set with !important
fail_html: Users cannot override this paragraph's line height with their own stylesheet.
pass_html: Users can override this paragraph's line height with their own stylesheet.
explanation: Inline spacing declared with !important blocks the user style overrides that WCAG 1.4.12 text spacing relies on.
how_to_test_manually: Apply a text spacing bookmarklet and check for clipped or overlapping text.

title: Clickable div that cannot receive keyboard focus
explanation: A div with a click handler is invisible to keyboard users. Use a real button, which is focusable and activates with Enter and Space. Axe does not flag this pattern.
how_to_test_manually: Unplug the mouse and try to reach and activate every interactive element.

title: Scrollable region that keyboard users cannot reach
fail_html:
Line one of the terms.

Line two of the terms.

Line three of the terms.

Line four of the terms.

Line five of the terms.
pass_html:
Line one of the terms.

Line two of the terms.

Line three of the terms.

Line four of the terms.

Line five of the terms.
explanation: A scrollable area with no focusable content cannot be scrolled with a keyboard in many browsers. Add tabindex=0 and a name so keyboard users can scroll it.
how_to_test_manually: Tab to the scrollable region and try to scroll with the arrow keys.

title: Page redirects automatically after five seconds
pass_html: Continue to the next page when you are ready.
explanation: Timed refreshes and redirects take control away from users who need more time to read. Give a link or button instead.
how_to_test_manually: Search for meta refresh tags and scripted redirects with timers.

title: Scrolling marquee text with no way to pause
explanation: The marquee element is obsolete and moves text without any control. Users with attention or reading disabilities cannot pause it.
how_to_test_manually: Find any moving, blinking, or scrolling content that lasts more than five seconds and confirm it can be paused.

title: No skip link, headings, or landmarks to bypass navigation
fail_html:
Home Products Contact

Welcome to the store.
pass_html:
Skip to main content
Home Products Contact

Welcome

Welcome to the store.
explanation: Keyboard users must tab through every repeated link on every page unless a skip link, headings, or landmarks give them a shortcut.
how_to_test_manually: Press Tab once on page load. A skip link should appear, or landmark navigation should be available.

title: Document has no title element
fail_html:
Contact us

Send us a message.
pass_html:
Contact us

Send us a message.
explanation: The page title is the first thing a screen reader announces and the label in browser tabs and history. Every page needs a unique, descriptive one.
how_to_test_manually: Read each page title out of context. It should identify the page and its site.

title: Positive tabindex values scramble the focus order
fail_html: Third in DOM, first in tab order Second in DOM Natural order
pass_html: First link Second link Third link
explanation: Positive tabindex values override the natural order and tend to produce focus sequences that no longer match the visual layout. Use tabindex 0 or -1 only.
how_to_test_manually: Tab through the page and compare the focus sequence to the visual reading order.

title: Icon-only link with no accessible name
explanation: A link with no text and no label is announced only as 'link', so its destination cannot be understood.
how_to_test_manually: List links with a screen reader and look for unnamed links.

title: Vague link text such as click here
explanation: Screen reader users often list all links on a page out of context. 'Click here' and 'read more' tell them nothing in that view.
how_to_test_manually: Open a links list in a screen reader and check that each link makes sense alone.

title: Empty heading element
explanation: An empty heading shows up in the heading outline as a blank entry and confuses people who navigate by heading.
how_to_test_manually: List all headings in a screen reader and look for empty entries.

title: Focus outline removed with no replacement
explanation: Removing the focus outline with outline:none and providing no alternative leaves keyboard users unable to see where they are. Axe cannot see this because it depends on styles in a focused state.
how_to_test_manually: Tab through the page and confirm every focus stop is visible.

title: Fixed cookie banner covers the focused footer link
fail_html:
Privacy policy
Cookie banner pinned to the bottom of the viewport
pass_html:
Privacy policy
Cookie banner pinned to the bottom of the viewport
explanation: New in WCAG 2.2. A focused control must not be completely hidden by author-created content such as a sticky header or cookie banner. When the focused link sits at the very end of the page, the browser cannot scroll it clear of a fixed banner unless the page leaves room (padding-bottom or scroll-padding). Automated rules do not test this.
how_to_test_manually: Tab and Shift+Tab through the page with sticky headers, cookie banners, and chat widgets visible.

title: Carousel that can only be operated by swiping
fail_html:
Product 1
Product 2
Product 3
pass_html: Product 1
explanation: Path-based gestures such as swiping must have a single-pointer alternative, such as previous and next buttons, for people who cannot perform them.
how_to_test_manually: Find gesture-driven widgets and check for a tap or click alternative.

title: Accessible name does not contain the visible label
explanation: Speech input users activate controls by saying the visible label. If the accessible name is 'Find products', saying 'click Search' fails. This is an experimental axe rule.
how_to_test_manually: Compare each visible label with the computed accessible name in browser developer tools.

title: List reordering available only by dragging
fail_html:
• Task A
  • Task B
  • Task C
pass_html:
• Task A
  • Task B
  • Task C
explanation: New in WCAG 2.2. Anything you can do by dragging must also be possible with a simple tap or click, for example with move up and move down buttons.
how_to_test_manually: Find drag and drop features and try to complete the task using single clicks only.

title: Tiny adjacent icon buttons under 24 by 24 pixels
explanation: New in WCAG 2.2. Targets should be at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels unless they have enough spacing. Two 16 pixel buttons two pixels apart fail on both size and spacing.
how_to_test_manually: Measure target size in developer tools and check spacing to neighboring targets.

title: Html element has no lang attribute
explanation: Screen readers pick a pronunciation engine from the page language. Without lang, English text may be read with the wrong accent or rules.
how_to_test_manually: Check the lang attribute on the html element of each template.

title: Html lang attribute has an invalid value
explanation: The lang attribute takes a BCP 47 language tag such as en or en-US, not a language name.
how_to_test_manually: Confirm lang uses a valid tag.

title: Foreign phrase without a lang attribute
fail_html: The French phrase c'est la vie means that is life.
pass_html: The French phrase c'est la vie means that is life.
explanation: A screen reader switches voice and pronunciation only when told a passage is in another language. Axe validates lang values that exist but cannot tell when one is missing.
how_to_test_manually: Look for foreign words and quotes in content and check they have a lang attribute.

title: Lang attribute on a passage has an invalid code
fail_html: The French phrase c'est la vie means that is life.
pass_html: The French phrase c'est la vie means that is life.
explanation: An invalid code on a nested element (here the language name instead of the code fr) is ignored, so the phrase is read with the wrong voice.
how_to_test_manually: Validate every lang attribute on the page.

title: Select that navigates away as soon as the value changes
fail_html: <label for="jump">Jump to</label> <select id="jump" onchange="void 0"><option value="">Choose a page</option><option value="/a">Pricing</option><option value="/b">Docs</option></select>
pass_html: <label for="jump">Jump to</label> <select id="jump"><option value="/a">Pricing</option><option value="/b">Docs</option></select> <button type="button">Go</button>
explanation: Keyboard and screen reader users change a select by moving through options, so an onchange that navigates fires before they finish choosing. Provide an explicit Go button.
how_to_test_manually: Change each control with the keyboard and confirm nothing navigates or submits until the user presses a button.

title: Invalid field indicated only by a red border
pass_html: Error: enter a 5 digit ZIP code, for example 90210.
explanation: A red border is invisible to people who cannot perceive color and says nothing to screen reader users. Errors need text, programmatic association, and ideally a suggestion.
how_to_test_manually: Submit the form with bad data using only a screen reader. Each error should be announced and tied to its field.

title: Input labeled only by placeholder text
explanation: Placeholder text disappears when the user types, has weak contrast in most designs, and is not a reliable label across assistive technologies. Use a visible label. Notably, axe-core 4.14 accepts a placeholder as an accessible name and does not report this pattern, so it is easy to miss in automated scans.
how_to_test_manually: Clear every field and check that each still has a visible, persistent label.

title: Billing form makes the user retype the shipping address
fail_html: <form><fieldset><legend>Shipping address</legend><label for="s1">Street</label> <input id="s1" type="text" autocomplete="shipping street-address"></fieldset><fieldset><legend>Billing address</legend><label for="b1">Street</label> <input id="b1" type="text" autocomplete="billing street-address"></fieldset></form>
pass_html: <form><fieldset><legend>Shipping address</legend><label for="s1">Street</label> <input id="s1" type="text" autocomplete="shipping street-address"></fieldset><label><input type="checkbox" checked> Billing address is the same as shipping</label></form>
explanation: New in WCAG 2.2. Do not ask users to re-enter information they already gave earlier in the same process. Auto-populate it or let them select it.
how_to_test_manually: Complete multi-step flows and flag any field that repeats earlier answers.

title: Password field blocks paste and password managers
explanation: New in WCAG 2.2. Authentication cannot depend on memorizing or transcribing a password unless the user can paste or use a password manager. Blocking paste is a direct failure.
how_to_test_manually: Try to sign in using a password manager and by pasting the password.

title: Icon-only button with no accessible name
fail_html: <button type="button"><svg aria-hidden="true" width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><path d="M2 2l12 12M14 2L2 14" stroke="#000" stroke-width="2"/></svg></button>
pass_html: <button type="button" aria-label="Close dialog"><svg aria-hidden="true" width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 16 16"><path d="M2 2l12 12M14 2L2 14" stroke="#000" stroke-width="2"/></svg></button>
explanation: A button with only an icon and no label is announced as just 'button'. This is one of the most frequent failures found in real audits.
how_to_test_manually: Tab through buttons with a screen reader and listen for unnamed ones.

title: Custom checkbox missing aria-checked
explanation: Custom widgets must expose required state attributes. Without aria-checked, a screen reader cannot tell if the box is on or off. A native input type=checkbox avoids the problem entirely.
how_to_test_manually: Operate each custom widget with a screen reader and confirm state changes are announced.

title: Misspelled ARIA role
explanation: An unknown role value is ignored, so the element loses the semantics the author intended. Prefer native elements to ARIA roles.
how_to_test_manually: Validate role values against the ARIA specification.

title: Select element without a label
explanation: A select without a label is announced as 'combo box' with no purpose.
how_to_test_manually: Check that every form control has a programmatic label.

title: Focusable link hidden with aria-hidden
explanation: Content with aria-hidden=true is removed from the accessibility tree, but keyboard users can still tab to focusable children, landing on controls that are never announced.
how_to_test_manually: Tab through the page with a screen reader and watch for silent focus stops.

title: Link nested inside a button
explanation: Interactive elements must not contain other interactive elements. Screen readers often cannot reach the inner control.
how_to_test_manually: Search for links inside buttons and buttons inside links.

title: Iframe without a title
pass_html: <iframe src="about:blank" width="320" height="120" title="Embedded map of our office location"></iframe>
explanation: Screen reader users hear the frame title when they enter a frame. Without one, they hear only 'frame'.
how_to_test_manually: List frames in a screen reader and check each has a descriptive title.

title: Misspelled ARIA attribute
explanation: A typo in an aria attribute name silently disables it, so state is never exposed.
how_to_test_manually: Validate ARIA attribute names.

title: ARIA attribute not allowed on the element's role
explanation: aria-checked is not supported on a button role. Use aria-pressed for toggle buttons.
how_to_test_manually: Compare each ARIA attribute with the allowed attributes for the element's role.

title: Custom textbox with no accessible name
explanation: Custom input widgets need an accessible name just like native inputs.
how_to_test_manually: Focus each custom input with a screen reader and confirm it announces a name.

title: Save confirmation injected without a live region
explanation: Dynamic messages are not announced unless they are in a live region. role=status is polite and does not move focus. Axe cannot detect a missing live region because it does not run your scripts.
how_to_test_manually: Trigger the message with a screen reader running and confirm it is announced.
